information.description:
Typically seen as leaders for entire sects of Wraiths, Goliaths are hulking brutes with tons of reclaimed cyberware, firepower, and combat drugs. They wade through small arms fire and hostile action alike, all to raid another convoy of medical supplies or laugh at torturing some helpless civvie. To put it simply, this is the most Wraith a Wraith gets.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Wraiths).

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.
Throwing hands, does not ignore half armor.

Cost: Half (Round Up) the original weapon’s Cost ♦ Availability: Price Category is unchanged

“We live in dangerous times. Violence is rampant, so everyone needs a way to defend themselves. Sadly, many can’t afford effective problem-solvers, which is where bootlegs come to save the day. Yeah, customizing ‘em is a pain and they fall apart easier, but look at that price tag!”

An Ironfake Variant Weapon becomes Exotic if it was not already so, is reduced to Poor Quality, and all of its BODY requirements (if any) are increased by 1 (e.g., BODY 10+ to not jam is now BODY 11+ to not jam). If the weapon was already Poor Quality, its Ironfake Variant now jams when rolling any 1 during the Attack Check (i.e., not negated by Fumble Recovery) and when it malfunctions, it requires an additional Action to clear the malfunction. An Ironfake Weapon cannot be bought using the CEMK’s rule of purchasing it at double its Cost to source it without a Fixer.

Exotic Poor Quality Machine Gun (w/ Power Rebuild). Holds 300 rounds, and is capable of Autofire (Machine Gun 5). Can only use Autofire and Suppressive Fire, both of which expend 20 rounds per use. Requires BODY 12+ to be wielded unless Mounted, and BODY 14+ to not reduce MOVE by 2 while wielded. Requires 3 Actions to Reload.

Variant of: Militech Mk. 31 HMG
Class: Exotic Poor Quality Machine Gun
Range: N/A
Pre-installed: Power Rebuild (effects already included in these stats)
Alt. fire: Autofire (Machine Gun 5), Suppressive Fire

Foundry notes:

  • Autofire and Suppressive Fire only; 2d6 is the standard Autofire damage.
  • Autofire only, so its DV table is the Autofire table.
  • Its range tables come from this module's DV Tables compendium; run the module's "Use Corgo's 77 DV Tables" macro once per world (see the module README).
  • Exotic weapon.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog > Variants).

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) for Subdermal Armors SP12 and lower.

Cost: 3,000eb (Luxury) for Subdermal Armors SP13 and higher.

A dense, layered microplating that boosts the stopping power of cybernetic armor, giving extra bite against blunt force and ballistics.

Skinweave/Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancement. Increases the enhanced armor’s SP by 1. Cannot increase the SP of Dragoon Plating.

NOTE: Credit to the From the Ashes LC for the idea on changes to this item.

Enhances: Skinweave or Subdermal Armor
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • Corgo prices this by the armor's SP, so it comes as two items.
  • Change the SP on the armor item by hand; an upgrade installed in cyberware can't do it.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > External Body Cyberware).
No immediate damage. If hit DV15 Resist Torture/Drugs Check. On a fail 3d6 damage to HP. No Ablation.

Primary Effect

Dose lasts for 10 Minutes.

  • Induces a state of frenzy and increased aggression
  • User takes no Bonus Damage for any Critical Injury
  • Wound State/Facedown penalties to Skill or Stat checks are halved*

Secondary Effect (DV17)

When the dose wears off, the user rolls WILL + Resist Torture/Drugs + 1d10 against Secondary DV.

  • -2 Humanity Loss.
  • User is now addicted to Berserker if not already addicted. +1 to Base Death Save Penalty while addicted.

*This is not supported by the system and must be manually adjusted.

Cyberarm Option. Provides a +1 Complementary Bonus to Autofire Checks made with weapons wielded in the hand of or installed within the Cyberarm. Multiple installations of this do not stack.

Foundry notes:

  • The +1 is situational because it only covers weapons in that arm: tick it in the roll dialog.
